problems.title: Static or dynamic?

parts.prompt: A vector holding Circles, Squares and Triangles drawn by a loop:
A tick handler whose strategy type is fixed per binary, in the hot path:

hints: Heterogeneous at run time, or known at compile time?
problems.solution: Heterogeneous collections need run-time dispatch; fixed strategies get inlined via templates.

problems.title: constexpr
problems.statement: constexpr int fib(int n) {...}, with int x = fib(30); inside main (not a constant expression context).

parts.prompt: Is it guaranteed to be computed at compile time?
options: No: constexpr permits, consteval or a constexpr variable forces

problems.solution: Write constexpr int x = fib(30); to force it.

problems.title: Virtual cost
problems.statement: A virtual call in a loop over 10⁶ objects of 4 random concrete types, about 15-cycle mispredict penalty, prediction rate about 25%.
problems.solution: About 11M cycles, several milliseconds at 3 GHz. Sorting by type turns this into near-perfect prediction.

problems.title: final
problems.statement: struct Fast final : Base { void f() override; }; void g(Fast& x) { x.f(); }

options: Yes: no class can derive from Fast

hints: What could the dynamic type be?
problems.solution: final pins the dynamic type, enabling a direct (inlinable) call.

problems.title: Templates in headers
problems.statement: A template function defined in a .cpp and only declared in the header, used from another .cpp.

options: link error: undefined reference (never instantiated for that type)
define it in the header, or explicitly instantiate the needed types in the .cpp

problems.solution: The compiler instantiates templates where they're used, so it needs the body there.

problems.title: std::function
problems.statement: Storing a lambda capturing 64 bytes in std::function (libstdc++ small buffer: 16 bytes).

options: Yes: the capture exceeds the small buffer

parts.prompt: Zero-cost alternative for a hot callback?
options: function pointer to the lambda (captures not allowed)

problems.solution: Template parameters keep the callable's type, so it can be inlined.

problems.title: Dependent base
problems.statement: Inside template <class T> struct D : B<T> { void g() { f(); } };, f is a member of B<T>.

options: No: f isn't found by unqualified lookup in a dependent base; write this->f()

problems.solution: Dependent bases aren't searched at definition time.

problems.title: Safe average
problems.statement: The integral safe_avg(a, b) = a/2 + b/2 + (a%2 + b%2)/2 with C++ truncating division.
problems.solution: 8; INT_MAX without overflow; −1 − 2 + 0 = −3 (the exact mean is −3.5, truncated toward zero). Compare std::midpoint.
